questions.question:
A company has an IAM role named Analytics in Account A (111111111111). The role has an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::reports-bucket/*. The reports-bucket bucket is in Account B (222222222222) and has a bucket policy that does not mention Account A. Objects are encrypted with SSE-S3. When the role tries to download an object, it receives an AccessDenied error.

What should a security engineer do to grant access while following the principle of least privilege?

options.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy in Account B that allows s3:GetObject on reports-bucket/* for the principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/Analytics.
Add a statement to the bucket policy in Account B that allows s3:GetObject on reports-bucket/* for the principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root.
Attach a permissions boundary to the Analytics role that allows s3:GetObject on reports-bucket/*.
Create an SCP in the organization that explicitly allows s3:GetObject on reports-bucket/* and attach it to Account A.

questions.explanation: En acceso entre cuentas se necesitan DOS permisos: la política de identidad en la cuenta del principal (ya existe) y la política de recurso en la cuenta dueña (falta). Conceder al ARN del rol es más restrictivo que a :root, que delega en cualquier principal de la cuenta A. Una SCP o un permissions boundary solo limitan; nunca otorgan permisos.

questions.question:
A security engineer has already updated a bucket policy in Account B so that a role in Account A can read objects. The bucket uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key that is in Account B. The role still receives AccessDenied when it calls GetObject. CloudTrail in Account B shows a kms:Decrypt denial.

Which combination of changes will resolve the issue?

options.text: Update only the role's identity-based policy in Account A to allow kms:Decrypt on the key ARN in Account B.
Update the key policy in Account B to allow kms:Decrypt for the role in Account A, and add kms:Decrypt on the key ARN to the role's identity-based policy in Account A.
Create a grant on the AWS managed key aws/s3 in Account B for the role in Account A.
Change the default encryption of the bucket to SSE-S3; existing objects will be re-encrypted automatically.

questions.explanation: Para usar una KMS key de otra cuenta, la key policy (cuenta B) debe permitir a la cuenta/rol externo Y la política de identidad del rol (cuenta A) debe permitir kms:Decrypt sobre el ARN de la key. Las AWS managed keys no se pueden compartir entre cuentas, y cambiar el cifrado por defecto no recifra objetos existentes.

questions.question:
A company wants to prevent all accounts in its organization from using any AWS Region other than us-east-1 and eu-west-1. A security engineer attaches an SCP that denies all actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not one of those two Regions. After the change, administrators can no longer manage IAM roles or view CloudFront distributions.

How should the engineer modify the SCP?

options.text: Attach the SCP to the management account only, so that member accounts can still use global services.
Change the deny statement to use NotAction and list the global services (for example, IAM, AWS STS, CloudFront, Route 53, and AWS Support) so they are exempt from the Region condition.
Add an Allow statement for iam:* and cloudfront:* to the same SCP, because an explicit allow overrides the Region deny.
Replace aws:RequestedRegion with ec2:Region so that the condition applies only to regional services.

questions.explanation: Los servicios globales envían sus solicitudes a un endpoint en us-east-1 u otra Región, por lo que un deny por Región puede bloquearlos. El patrón documentado es Deny + NotAction con los servicios globales exentos. Un Allow nunca anula un Deny explícito, y las SCP no afectan a la cuenta de administración.

questions.question:
An organization has an SCP attached to the root OU that denies s3:DeleteBucket. A developer who has the AdministratorAccess policy in the organization's management account successfully deletes a bucket.

What is the reason?

options.text: SCPs apply only to IAM roles, not to IAM users.
SCPs do not affect users or roles in the management account.
AdministratorAccess includes an explicit allow that overrides SCPs.
SCPs attached to the root OU are inherited only by nested OUs, not by accounts directly under the root.

questions.explanation: Las SCP nunca restringen a la cuenta de administración; por eso AWS recomienda no ejecutar cargas de trabajo en ella. Las SCP sí aplican a usuarios y roles (incluido root) de las cuentas miembro, y se heredan por todas las cuentas bajo el root.

questions.question:
In a single AWS account, an IAM user has no identity-based policies attached. A bucket policy on a bucket in the same account allows s3:GetObject for the user's ARN. No SCPs, permissions boundaries, or session policies apply.

What happens when the user calls GetObject on an object in the bucket?

options.text: The request is denied because the user needs an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject.
The request is allowed only if the object ACL also grants READ to the user.
The request is denied because bucket policies can grant access only to other AWS accounts.
The request is allowed because, within the same account, an allow in the resource-based policy is sufficient.

questions.explanation: Dentro de la misma cuenta, la evaluación es una unión: basta con un Allow en la política de identidad O en la de recurso (si no hay Deny explícito). Entre cuentas, en cambio, se requieren ambos.

questions.question:
A company wants developers to create IAM roles for their AWS Lambda functions without the involvement of the security team. The security team must ensure that developers cannot create roles with more permissions than an approved policy named DevBoundary, and that developers cannot escalate their own privileges.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Allow iam:CreateRole for developers and use an AWS Config rule to delete roles that have AdministratorAccess attached.
Create an SCP that allows iam:CreateRole only for the developers' OU and denies iam:AttachRolePolicy.
Attach DevBoundary as a permissions boundary to the developers' IAM users and allow iam:* actions.
Allow iam:CreateRole and iam:PutRolePolicy only when the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition key equals the DevBoundary ARN, and deny changes to DevBoundary and the removal of permissions boundaries.

questions.explanation: El patrón de delegación segura exige el boundary en cada rol creado (condición iam:PermissionsBoundary) y protege el boundary: deny de iam:CreatePolicyVersion/DeletePolicy sobre DevBoundary y de iam:DeleteRolePermissionsBoundary. Un boundary solo en los desarrolladores no limita los roles que crean, y Config es detectivo, no preventivo.

questions.question:
An IAM role has the AWS managed policy AdministratorAccess attached. The role also has a permissions boundary that allows only s3:* and cloudwatch:*. An SCP on the account allows all actions except cloudwatch:DeleteAlarms.

Which actions can the role perform? (Select TWO.)

options.text: ec2:DescribeInstances
cloudwatch:PutMetricAlarm
iam:CreateUser
cloudwatch:DeleteAlarms
s3:PutObject

questions.explanation: Los permisos efectivos son la intersección de identidad, boundary y SCP. EC2 e IAM quedan fuera del boundary, y DeleteAlarms lo niega la SCP. Solo S3 y las acciones de CloudWatch no denegadas sobreviven.

questions.question:
A company uses ABAC for EC2. Engineers can start and stop only the instances whose project tag matches their aws:PrincipalTag/project. The security team discovered that an engineer gained access to another project's instances by changing the instance tag.

Which actions should the security engineer take to prevent this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Deny ec2:CreateTags and ec2:DeleteTags on existing instances unless ec2:ResourceTag/project matches aws:PrincipalTag/project and aws:RequestTag/project also matches aws:PrincipalTag/project.
Use a tag policy in AWS Organizations to make the project tag key case-sensitive.
Require that the aws:RequestTag/project key in ec2:RunInstances equals aws:PrincipalTag/project, and restrict the allowed tag keys with aws:TagKeys.
Enable AWS Config to record tag changes on EC2 instances.
Replace the ABAC policy with one inline policy per engineer that lists instance IDs.

questions.explanation: ABAC depende de que los tags no puedan manipularse: hay que controlar quién crea o cambia tags (ResourceTag/RequestTag/TagKeys) y exigir el tag correcto al crear. Config solo detecta, y las tag policies estandarizan valores pero no impiden el cambio de un tag permitido.

questions.question:
A company federates its workforce into AWS through SAML 2.0. To implement ABAC, the identity provider now sends the attribute https://aws.amazon.com/SAML/Attributes/PrincipalTag:costcenter. After the change, all federated sign-ins fail with an AccessDenied error on AssumeRoleWithSAML.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Add an iam:TagRole permission to the identity-based policy of the role.
Add the aws:RequestTag/costcenter condition to the SAML provider metadata document.
Add the sts:TagSession action to the trust policy of the role that federated users assume.
Enable the costcenter tag as a cost allocation tag in AWS Billing.

questions.explanation: Para pasar session tags al asumir un rol, la trust policy debe permitir sts:TagSession además de la acción de assume. Sin ese permiso, la solicitud que incluye tags falla.

questions.question:
A company grants a third-party monitoring vendor access to its account through an IAM role. The vendor uses the same AWS account to access the accounts of many customers. The company wants to make sure that another customer of the vendor cannot trick the vendor into accessing the company's account.

What should the security engineer add to the role's trust policy?

options.text: A condition that requires aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent to be true.
A condition that requires a unique sts:ExternalId value that the vendor generates for the company.
A condition on aws:SourceArn that matches the vendor's account ARN.
A condition on aws:PrincipalOrgID that matches the company's organization ID.

questions.explanation: Es el problema del confused deputy entre cuentas: el external ID único por cliente impide que otro cliente del proveedor haga que este asuma el rol equivocado. aws:SourceArn aplica a service principals; MFA no aplica a un proceso automatizado; PrincipalOrgID no sirve porque el proveedor está fuera de la organización.

questions.question:
A security engineer discovers that temporary credentials for an IAM role used by an application on EC2 were exfiltrated. The role must remain available to the application, and the engineer must invalidate the stolen credentials as quickly as possible.

Which action should the engineer take FIRST?

options.text: Rotate the access keys of the role in the IAM console.
Use the Revoke active sessions option for the role, which adds a policy that denies all actions for sessions issued before the current time (aws:TokenIssueTime).
Detach all policies from the role until the investigation is complete.
Delete the role and re-create it with the same name and policies.

questions.explanation: Las credenciales temporales no se pueden revocar individualmente, pero la revocación de sesiones niega todo a los tokens emitidos antes de cierta hora. La aplicación vuelve a obtener credenciales nuevas del instance profile. Los roles no tienen access keys, y borrar o vaciar el rol interrumpe el servicio.

questions.question:
A script uses credentials from role A to assume role B. Role B has a maximum session duration of 8 hours. The script calls AssumeRole with DurationSeconds set to 14400 (4 hours), and the call fails with a validation error.

What is the cause?

options.text: Role chaining limits the session duration to a maximum of 1 hour, regardless of the role's maximum session duration.
Role B must have MFA required in its trust policy to allow sessions longer than 1 hour.
DurationSeconds cannot exceed 3600 unless the role trust policy includes sts:SetSourceIdentity.
The maximum session duration of role A must also be at least 4 hours.

questions.explanation: Cuando se asume un rol usando credenciales de otro rol (role chaining), la sesión resultante tiene como máximo 1 hora.

questions.question:
An S3 bucket is configured to send event notifications to an SNS topic in the same account. The security engineer must update the topic's access policy so that only that specific bucket can publish to the topic, preventing a confused deputy problem.

Which policy statement should be used?

options.text: Allow sns:Publish to the service principal s3.amazonaws.com with a condition on sts:ExternalId.
Allow sns:Publish to the principal arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:root with a condition on aws:SourceVpce.
Allow sns:Publish to the service principal s3.amazonaws.com with conditions on aws:SourceArn (the bucket ARN) and aws:SourceAccount (the account ID).
Allow sns:Publish to * with a condition on aws:PrincipalOrgID.

questions.explanation: Cuando un servicio de AWS actúa en tu nombre, se limita con aws:SourceArn y aws:SourceAccount, que es la mitigación del confused deputy entre servicios. sts:ExternalId es para roles asumidos por terceros, y PrincipalOrgID no aplica a service principals.

questions.question:
A company has more than 300 accounts in AWS Organizations, and accounts are added every week. A central S3 bucket must be readable by any IAM principal in the organization and by no one else.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Add a bucket policy statement that allows s3:GetObject to Principal "*" with the condition aws:PrincipalOrgID equal to the organization ID.
Create a role in the bucket's account and require all accounts to assume it through role chaining.
Add every account ID to the Principal element of the bucket policy and update it with a Lambda function when accounts are created.
Use S3 ACLs to grant READ to the canonical user ID of each account in the organization.

questions.explanation: aws:PrincipalOrgID limita el acceso a principales de la organización y se actualiza solo al agregar cuentas. Las ACLs están desaconsejadas (Object Ownership: bucket owner enforced).

questions.question:
The trust policy of a role in Account B contains "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root"} and allows sts:AssumeRole.

Which statement correctly describes who can assume the role?

options.text: Only principals in account 111111111111 that have signed in with MFA.
Any IAM user or role in account 111111111111, even without an identity-based policy that allows sts:AssumeRole.
Only the root user of account 111111111111.
Any IAM user or role in account 111111111111 whose identity-based policies allow sts:AssumeRole on the role.

questions.explanation: :root en Principal delega la decisión en la cuenta A: cualquier principal de esa cuenta al que su administrador le permita sts:AssumeRole. No se refiere solo al usuario root.

questions.question:
A company uses IAM Access Analyzer with the organization as the zone of trust. The analyzer generates an active finding for a bucket that is intentionally shared with a partner's AWS account (444444444444). The security team wants to stop seeing findings for this intended access but continue to be notified about any other external access.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Disable Access Analyzer findings for Amazon S3 in the analyzer settings.
Add account 444444444444 to the organization so the access is no longer external.
Delete the analyzer and create a new analyzer with the account as the zone of trust.
Create an archive rule that matches findings where the resource is the bucket and the external principal is account 444444444444.

questions.explanation: Las archive rules archivan automáticamente hallazgos que coinciden con criterios de acceso esperado, sin perder visibilidad sobre nuevos accesos externos.

questions.question:
A security team must identify IAM roles, IAM user passwords, and access keys that have not been used in the last 90 days, as well as permissions that roles have but never use, across all accounts in the organization.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer for the organization.
Enable AWS Config in all accounts and use the iam-user-unused-credentials-check managed rule.
Create an IAM Access Analyzer unused access analyzer for the organization with a 90-day tracking period.
Download the IAM credential report from each account and combine them with Amazon Athena.

questions.explanation: El analizador de acceso no usado reporta roles, credenciales y permisos no usados de forma centralizada. El credential report es por cuenta y no cubre permisos no usados de roles; el analizador externo detecta accesos públicos o entre cuentas.

questions.question:
A development team has an IAM role with broad permissions for a new application. After the application has run in production for 30 days, the security team wants to replace the role's policy with a least-privilege policy based on the actions the application actually used.

Which approach should the security engineer use?

options.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation, which analyzes the role's CloudTrail activity and generates a policy template.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to recommend actions to remove from the role.
Use the IAM policy simulator to test every action in the current policy.
Use IAM Access Analyzer policy validation to remove unused actions from the policy.

questions.explanation: La generación de políticas de Access Analyzer usa la actividad registrada en CloudTrail para crear una política basada en el uso real. La validación revisa sintaxis y buenas prácticas, y el simulador prueba permisos pero no genera políticas.

questions.question:
A company deploys IAM policies through a CI/CD pipeline. The security team wants the pipeline to fail automatically if a new or updated policy grants iam:PassRole or s3:DeleteBucket.

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Add a step that runs the IAM Access Analyzer CheckAccessNotGranted custom policy check against each policy.
Create an SCP that denies iam:PassRole and s3:DeleteBucket in all accounts.
Add a step that runs IAM Access Analyzer ValidatePolicy and fails on ERROR findings.
Create an AWS Config rule that flags policies with iam:PassRole.

questions.explanation: CheckAccessNotGranted verifica que una política no conceda acciones específicas y se integra en pipelines. ValidatePolicy revisa sintaxis y buenas prácticas, no acciones concretas; Config detecta después del despliegue; una SCP bloquearía el uso legítimo en toda la cuenta.

questions.question:
A security engineer must require MFA for any ec2:StopInstances or ec2:TerminateInstances call made by IAM users. The policy must also block these calls when they are made with long-term access keys without MFA.

Which condition should the Deny statement use?

options.text: "Null": {"aws:MultiFactorAuthAge": "false"}
"Bool": {"aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent": "false"}
"Bool": {"aws:SecureTransport": "false"}
"BoolIfExists": {"aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent": "false"}

questions.explanation: Las solicitudes firmadas con access keys de largo plazo no incluyen la clave aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent. Con Bool la condición no coincide y el Deny no se aplica; con BoolIfExists, la ausencia de la clave también activa el Deny.

questions.question:
IAM users must use MFA for privileged actions from the AWS CLI. The users already have virtual MFA devices and access keys.

How should the users obtain credentials that satisfy MFA-protected policies?

options.text: Generate a new access key pair after signing in to the console with MFA.
Add the MFA serial number to the ~/.aws/config file without calling AWS STS.
Call sts get-session-token with the --serial-number and --token-code parameters and use the returned temporary credentials.
Call sts get-caller-identity with the MFA code to activate MFA on the access key.

questions.explanation: GetSessionToken con el código MFA devuelve credenciales temporales en las que aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent es true. (Con un perfil que asume un rol, mfa_serial en la config hace la llamada a STS automáticamente.)

questions.question:
An auditor asks for evidence of every IAM user in an account whose access keys have not been rotated in more than 90 days, including when each key was last used.

What is the MOST efficient way to obtain this information?

options.text: Query CloudTrail for CreateAccessKey events from the last 90 days.
Generate and download the IAM credential report for the account.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to list all IAM users in the account.
Run IAM Access Analyzer policy validation on each user's policies.

questions.explanation: El credential report lista todos los usuarios con estado de contraseña, MFA, fecha de rotación y último uso de cada access key.

questions.question:
A mobile application signs users in with an Amazon Cognito user pool. Each user must be able to upload files directly to an S3 bucket, but only under a prefix that belongs to that user.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use the user pool ID token as a bearer token in direct S3 PUT requests.
Grant the user pool app client permission to call s3:PutObject in the bucket policy.
Use a Cognito identity pool to exchange the user pool token for temporary AWS credentials, and use the ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub} policy variable in the authenticated role's policy.
Create an IAM user for each application user and store the access keys in the mobile application.

questions.explanation: El user pool autentica; el identity pool entrega credenciales AWS temporales. La variable de política con el identity ID limita a cada usuario a su propio prefijo. S3 no acepta tokens JWT de Cognito directamente.

questions.question:
An identity pool maps all authenticated users to one IAM role. The company now needs administrators (members of the user pool group Admins) to receive a role with more permissions, while other users keep the standard role.

What should the security engineer configure?

options.text: Assign an IAM role to the Admins group in the user pool and configure the identity pool to choose the role from the token (cognito:preferred_role).
Use a Lambda authorizer in the identity pool to return the role ARN.
Add an aws:PrincipalTag/Admins condition to the trust policy of the standard role.
Create a second identity pool for administrators and a separate mobile application.

questions.explanation: Los grupos del user pool pueden tener un rol IAM; con 'Choose role from token' el identity pool usa cognito:preferred_role del token. También existen reglas de mapeo basadas en claims.

questions.question:
A REST API in Amazon API Gateway must accept only requests from users who signed in to a Cognito user pool. The company wants to avoid writing custom authorization code.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a Lambda authorizer that calls the Cognito AdminGetUser API for every request.
Configure a Cognito user pool authorizer on the API methods so that API Gateway validates the JWT in the Authorization header.
Use an API key per user and store the key as a custom attribute in the user pool.
Configure IAM authorization on the API methods and send the user pool ID token as the SigV4 signature.

questions.explanation: El autorizador de Cognito user pool valida firma, expiración y emisor del token sin código. Un Lambda authorizer requiere código, y las API keys no autentican usuarios.

questions.question:
A company's consumer application uses a Cognito user pool. The security team detects credential-stuffing attempts that use leaked passwords from other websites.

Which features should the security engineer enable to reduce the risk? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Unauthenticated (guest) access in the identity pool.
Multi-factor authentication for user pool users.
A longer refresh token expiration.
Case-insensitive usernames.
Cognito threat protection (compromised-credentials detection and adaptive authentication).

questions.explanation: La protección contra amenazas de Cognito detecta credenciales filtradas y aplica autenticación adaptativa según el riesgo; MFA impide el acceso solo con contraseña. Las otras opciones no mitigan el ataque.

questions.question:
An application running on AWS Lambda generates S3 presigned URLs with an expiration of 7 days. Users report that the URLs stop working after a few hours.

What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The bucket policy must include the s3:signatureAge condition to allow 7-day URLs.
SigV4 presigned URLs cannot be valid for more than 12 hours.
S3 limits presigned URLs created by Lambda to 1 hour.
The URLs are signed with the temporary credentials of the Lambda execution role, so they become invalid when those credentials expire.

questions.explanation: Una URL prefirmada nunca dura más que las credenciales que la firmaron: con credenciales temporales de un rol, expira cuando expira la sesión aunque se pida más. El máximo con SigV4 es 7 días.

questions.question:
A security engineer discovers that an IAM user generated presigned URLs for confidential objects and shared them externally. The URLs are still within their expiration time.

What is the FASTEST way to make all of these URLs stop working?

options.text: Rotate the bucket's SSE-S3 encryption key.
Enable S3 Block Public Access on the bucket.
Remove the s3:GetObject permission from the IAM user (or deactivate the access key used to sign the URLs).
Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket.

questions.explanation: Una URL prefirmada actúa con los permisos de quien la firmó. Si se le retiran los permisos o se desactiva la clave que firmó, la URL deja de funcionar. Block Public Access no afecta solicitudes firmadas.

questions.question:
A SaaS company is building a document management application. The company needs fine-grained authorization rules such as "a user can edit a document only if the user belongs to the document's team and the document is not locked." The rules must be managed outside the application code and audited centrally.

Which AWS service should the company use?

options.text: Amazon Verified Permissions with policies written in Cedar.
Amazon Cognito user pool groups.
IAM identity-based policies with a policy per application user.
AWS IAM Identity Center permission sets.

questions.explanation: Verified Permissions externaliza la autorización de aplicaciones propias con políticas Cedar evaluadas por solicitud. IAM autoriza acceso a APIs de AWS, no a recursos de la aplicación.

questions.question: Match each Amazon Verified Permissions concept with its description.

options.text: Container for the policies and schema of one application
Role that the application assumes to call AWS APIs
Policy with placeholders for principal or resource that is linked to create policies
Defines entity types, attributes, and actions
Integration that maps users from a provider such as Cognito into principals

questions.explanation: Son los componentes básicos de Verified Permissions. El rol IAM no forma parte del modelo de autorización Cedar.

questions.question:
A company wants employees to sign in to IAM Identity Center with their on-premises Active Directory credentials. The company does not want to store users or password hashes in AWS or run domain controllers in AWS.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy AWS Managed Microsoft AD and create a one-way trust to the on-premises domain.
Use Simple AD and synchronize the users from on premises.
Use AD Connector as the identity source for IAM Identity Center.
Create IAM users that match each Active Directory username.

questions.explanation: AD Connector es un proxy hacia el AD existente: no almacena usuarios ni requiere controladores en AWS. AWS Managed Microsoft AD sí despliega controladores de dominio.

questions.question:
A company is migrating Windows workloads and Amazon RDS for SQL Server databases that require Windows authentication to AWS. Users exist in the on-premises Active Directory, and the workloads in AWS must keep working if the on-premises connection fails.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy AWS Managed Microsoft AD in AWS and create a trust relationship with the on-premises domain.
Use Amazon Cognito user pools with a SAML federation to Active Directory.
Use AD Connector to proxy all authentication requests to the on-premises domain.
Use IAM Roles Anywhere to authenticate the Windows workloads.

questions.explanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD ofrece un AD real en AWS (unión a dominio, RDS SQL Server con autenticación Windows) y puede funcionar aunque falle el enlace. Con AD Connector todo depende de la conectividad con on-premises.

questions.question:
A company has 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. A team of database administrators needs the same set of permissions in 25 of those accounts. Users sign in through an external identity provider.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an SCP that grants the DBA permissions and attach it to the 25 accounts.
Use IAM Identity Center: create a permission set for the DBAs and assign it to the DBA group in the 25 accounts.
Create an IAM role in each of the 25 accounts and a SAML provider in each account.
Create IAM users for each DBA in a central account and allow them to assume roles in the 25 accounts.

questions.explanation: Identity Center provisiona automáticamente roles en cada cuenta a partir del permission set y centraliza las asignaciones. Las SCP no conceden permisos.

questions.question:
A company uses Microsoft Entra ID as the identity provider for IAM Identity Center. When employees join or leave, administrators must manually create and remove users in Identity Center.

How can the company automate this process?

options.text: Configure a Lambda function that calls CreateUser in IAM for each new employee.
Configure an AD Connector pointing to Microsoft Entra ID.
Change the identity source to the Identity Center directory and import users with a CSV file.
Enable automatic provisioning with SCIM between Microsoft Entra ID and IAM Identity Center.

questions.explanation: SCIM sincroniza usuarios y grupos desde el IdP externo hacia Identity Center. SAML cubre la autenticación, pero no el aprovisionamiento.

questions.question:
A company runs scripts on on-premises servers that upload files to Amazon S3 with long-term IAM user access keys. The company has an internal certificate authority that issues X.509 certificates to every server. The security team wants to eliminate long-term credentials.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use IAM Roles Anywhere with a trust anchor for the internal CA, a profile that references an IAM role, and the credential helper on each server.
Store the access keys in AWS Secrets Manager and rotate them every 30 days.
Install the SSM Agent on each server and use the instance profile of a hybrid activation for S3 access.
Create a Cognito identity pool with unauthenticated access for the servers.

questions.explanation: Roles Anywhere intercambia un certificado X.509 de una CA de confianza por credenciales temporales de un rol, sin claves de largo plazo. Rotar claves sigue dejando credenciales de largo plazo.

questions.question:
A company uses IAM Roles Anywhere. Many servers have certificates from the same CA, but only servers whose certificate Common Name is backup-server must be able to assume the Backup role.

How should the security engineer restrict access?

options.text: Create a separate trust anchor for each server.
Add the certificate serial number to the Principal element of the trust policy.
Add a condition to the role's trust policy on aws:PrincipalTag/x509Subject/CN equal to backup-server.
Add an aws:SourceIp condition with the server IP addresses to the profile.

questions.explanation: Roles Anywhere expone atributos del certificado (subject, issuer, SAN) como principal tags que se usan en condiciones de la trust policy.

questions.question: A security engineer is configuring IAM Roles Anywhere for an on-premises server. Order the steps.

options.text: Create a trust anchor that references the certificate authority
Create an IAM role whose trust policy allows rolesanywhere.amazonaws.com
Create a profile that references the role
Configure the credential helper on the server with the certificate, private key, and ARNs

questions.explanation: Primero la confianza (CA), luego el rol que se asumirá, el profile que lo vincula y por último el cliente que obtiene credenciales.

questions.question: Order how AWS evaluates the policy types for a request made by a role session within a single account, from the first evaluation to the last.

options.text: Explicit Deny statements in any policy
AWS Organizations SCPs
Resource-based policies
Identity-based policies
Permissions boundaries

questions.explanation: Según la lógica de evaluación documentada: primero cualquier Deny explícito, luego SCP (y RCP), políticas de recurso, de identidad, permissions boundaries y finalmente session policies.

questions.question: Order the steps for a mobile app user to obtain temporary AWS credentials with Amazon Cognito.

options.text: The user authenticates against the user pool
The app receives the ID token from the user pool
The app sends the token to the identity pool
The identity pool obtains temporary credentials from AWS STS for the mapped IAM role
The app calls AWS services with the temporary credentials

questions.explanation: User pool = autenticación (tokens); identity pool = intercambio por credenciales AWS temporales del rol mapeado.

questions.question: Match each condition key with the use case it best addresses.

options.text: Deny sessions issued before a compromise
Restrict which resource a service principal acts on behalf of
Require MFA for sensitive API calls
Allow access only to principals in your organization
Require encryption in transit
Prevent the confused deputy problem with a third-party vendor

questions.explanation: Cada clave de condición resuelve un problema distinto; el cifrado en tránsito se exige con aws:SecureTransport.

questions.question: Match each requirement with the MOST appropriate AWS identity service.

prompts.text: Workforce single sign-on to many AWS accounts
Sign-up and sign-in for customers of a mobile app
On-premises workloads with X.509 certificates need AWS credentials
Fine-grained permissions inside a custom application

options.text: IAM Roles Anywhere
AWS Managed Microsoft AD
IAM users with long-term access keys
IAM Identity Center
Amazon Cognito user pools
Amazon Verified Permissions

questions.explanation: Cada servicio cubre un tipo de identidad distinto: fuerza laboral, clientes, cargas on-premises, autorización de la aplicación y AD.

questions.question:
A security engineer is reviewing an IAM policy attached to a developer role. All statements apply to Resource "*".

Which permissions could allow the developer to escalate privileges? (Select THREE.)

options.text: iam:PassRole together with ec2:RunInstances
iam:GenerateCredentialReport
iam:ListRoles
iam:AttachRolePolicy
iam:GetPolicy
iam:CreatePolicyVersion

questions.explanation: Crear una nueva versión por defecto de una política, adjuntar políticas a un rol o pasar un rol privilegiado a una instancia propia permiten obtener más permisos. Las acciones de lectura no lo permiten.

questions.question: A user in Account A must assume a role in Account B. Which conditions must be met? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The user has MFA enabled.
The role in Account B has a permissions boundary.
An identity-based policy in Account A allows the user to call sts:AssumeRole on the role ARN.
The trust policy of the role in Account B allows the user (or Account A) as a principal for sts:AssumeRole.
An SCP in Account B explicitly allows sts:AssumeRole.

questions.explanation: El assume entre cuentas requiere confianza en el destino (trust policy) y permiso en el origen (identity policy). Las SCP no conceden permisos; MFA solo si la trust policy lo exige.

questions.question:
A company wants to know which human user performed actions after assuming a shared role, even across role chaining. CloudTrail currently shows only the role session name, which users can set to any value.

What should the security engineer implement?

options.text: Add the aws:PrincipalTag/username tag to each role.
Enable CloudTrail data events for AWS STS.
Require sts:SourceIdentity in the role trust policies and have the identity provider set it to the user's corporate username.
Require a specific role session name pattern with an aws:userid condition.

questions.explanation: Source identity se establece al asumir el rol, no se puede cambiar en la sesión, persiste en el role chaining y queda en CloudTrail. Requiere sts:SetSourceIdentity en la trust policy.
